title: Engineering Elastic Nano- and Micro-Patterns and Textures for Directed Cell Motility
protocol: Place hPDMS molds face-up atop regular PDMS blocks.
Apply a 5-7 μL droplet of fluorescently labeled biotinylated protein solution between the hPDMS molding surface and clean pre-baked coverglass.
Apply approximately 7 μL of PAA premix droplet between the 3-(trimethoxysilyl) propyl methacrylate-coated glass-bottom Petri dish and rinsed, dried protein-coated hPDMS mold.
Incubate the PAA “sandwich” for 5 minutes.
Immerse the cured PAA sandwich in deionized water or Q-water at room temperature (20-25°C) for 30 minutes or at +4°C for 8-24 hours.
Place glass-bottom Petri dishes with Q-water into an ultrasonication chamber for 10-30 seconds to release the hPDMS molds from the PAA gel.
If necessary, gently peel the hPDMS mold manually if it is not released automatically.
Examine the nano-textured soft PAA surface for quality and defects using 3D microscopy.
Use hard PDMS instead of regular PDMS for the experiment.
Plasma-treat rectangular cover-glasses for 2 minutes before casting hPDMS.
Place a 5-7 μl droplet of hPDMS between passivated master mold and plasma-treated cover-glass.
Bake at 70°C for 30 min to cure the hPDMS.
Gently peel the cured molding cast off the master mold together with its bearing base.
Cut the peeled molding casts into 1✕1 cm squares by diamond pencil scribbling on the reverse side of nano-surface.
Put a 5-7 μL droplet of protein of interest solution atop of the hPDMS mold.
Cover the droplet with a round 15 mm pre-baked cover-glass in the "sandwich" fashion to ensure even distribution and economize the use of protein solution.
Incubate at 20-25°C for 40 minutes or at +4°C for 8-12 hours in a wet chamber.
Degas streptavidin-conjugated polyacrylamide premix not greater than 0.5 mL in a vacuum chamber or ultrasonication water bath for 1 hour.
Add TEMED after the degassing session.
Activate glass-bottom 35 mm Petri dishes using 3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl methacrylate.
Mix 100 μL of 3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl methacrylate with 20 mL of absolute ethyl alcohol.
Add 600 μL of 10% acetic acid to the mixture and mix well.
Incubate Petri dishes for 3 minutes.
Rinse Petri dishes with ethanol.
Dry Petri dishes immediately after rinsing.
Mix the desired volume of PAA premix with ammonium persulfate solution.
Place the mixed PAA premix as a single droplet between protein-coated casting mold and activated glass-bottom Petri dishes.
Incubate for PAA curing for 1 to 5 minutes.
Submerge resultant textured PAA nano-chip in cold deionized water for 8 to 10 hours.
Gently peel molding casts from the polymerized PAA surface with sharp tweezers.
Apply gentle pressure in the middle of the glass-bottom of the Petri dish to generate a dome-like deformation directed inward of the Petri dish.
Optionally, ultrasonicate hypotonically treated PAA "sandwiches" in a water bath at 37°C for 10 seconds.
Ensure careful peeling to prevent structural damage to the PAA nano-texture surface.
Repeat the PAA premix degassing procedure before casting the PAA nano-topographic surfaces.
Place released PAA nano-textures into isotonic PBS solution for 5 minutes to reverse PAA hypotonic swelling and check for surface quality under the microscope.
Store PAA nano-textured surfaces at +4°C in the dark for several weeks.
Optionally, add 0.01% sodium azide as a protein preservative to prevent bacterial contamination of the protein-coated PAA surfaces.
Incubate successfully released PAA nano-textures with 200 μg/mL ICAM1-Fc solution in cold PBS at 4°C for 8-12 hours.
Rinse incubated PAA nano-textures with cold PBS and immediately use for T cell adhesion and contact guidance assays.
Store ICAM1-coated PAA surfaces at +4°C in the dark for up to a week.
Spread a thin submillimeter layer of hPDMS premix atop the molding matrix passivated surface manually or by spin-coating.
Cure the hPDMS layer at approximately 70°C for 30 minutes.
Pour regular PDMS (rPDMS) premix layer on top of the hPDMS layer to achieve a final stamp thickness of approximately 7 mm and cure it at approximately 7°C for 1 hour.
Peel off the cured composite PDMS gently from the matrix.
Cut the peeled-off PDMS into pieces sized around 0.5-1 cm².
Prepare two rectangular cover glasses and label them accordingly.
Coat the composite nano-stamps with 5-7 μL of protein solution (fluorescent, biotinylated) by sandwiching it between the stamp’s surface and a clean coverglass in the wet chamber.
Incubate the protein-coated stamps at 20-25°C or +4°C for at least 40 minutes or up to 8-12 hours respectively.
Rinse and dry the protein-coated nano-stamps.
Place the rinsed and dried nano-stamps on the rectangular cover-glass.
Align the nano-stamps either vertically or horizontally with respect to the cover-glass edges.
Clean dust-free cover-glass pieces with Scotch-Tape™.
Immobilize the cleaned cover-glass pieces on glass-slides using Scotch-Tape™.
Gently place the protein-coated nano-stamp onto the immobilized cover-glass piece, ensuring alignment with the edges of the glass-slide.
Place a weight (∼100 g) atop the nano-stamp to ensure proper contact.
Remove the weight and nano-stamp together in one movement.
Repeat steps 4-9 for dual protein grid printing with orthogonal orientation.
Apply 5-7 μL of PAA premix between the coated glass-bottom Petri dish and the nano-patterned cover-glass.
Incubate at room temperature (∼20-25°C) for ∼5 minutes to polymerize the PAA gel.
Fill the Petri dish with Q-water and incubate for 30 minutes at 20-25°C or at +4°C for 8-24 hours.
Ultrasonicate the Petri dishes briefly (10-30 seconds).
Peel off the cover-glass pieces from the PAA gels.
Inspect the microscopy images of the nano-patterns for quality.
Coat silanized plastic nano-surface or silicone crystal matrix with ≤0.5 mm hPDMS gently spreading it with soft Parafilm-made spatula.
Cure matrix at 70°C for 30 minutes.
Pour rPDMS atop of the hPDMS to reach a final thickness of 8 mm.
Cure at 70°C for ∼1 hour.
Peel composite nano-stamps from the master matrix.
Cut nano-stamps into 5✕5 mm or 1✕1 cm pieces.
Place 5 μL droplets of a 0.2 mg/mL solution of biotin- and fluorophore-labelled protein of interest atop the 5×5 mm or 1×1 cm square nano-stamps.
Sandwich the protein solution droplet between the stamp’s printing surface and a pre-baked 15 mm round glass coverslip.
Incubate the nano-stamps with the “sandwiched” droplet of protein solution for 40 minutes at 20-25°C or overnight at +4°C in a wet chamber.
Rinse the nano-stamps gently in deionized milli-Q water after incubation.
Dry the nano-stamps gently under a jet of filtered air, nitrogen, or argon.
Print nano-patterns on “intermediate” cover-glass surface using nano-stamps pre-coated with protein of interest.

Transfer biotin-conjugated protein micro- and nano-patterns from the intermediate substrate onto hydrogels by cross-linking patterned proteins’ biotin tags to streptavidin-conjugated polyacrylamide (PAA).
Mix Alexa Fluor™ 568 fluorophore- and biotin-prelabeled anti-collagen rabbit pAb with the appropriate buffer.
Mix Alexa Fluor™ 488 fluorophore- and biotin-prelabeled Fab fragments of anti-Fcγ antibody with the appropriate buffer.
Align the nano-stamps’ nano-lines features directionality to the edges of the rectangular “loading” cover-glass.
Attach the nano-stamps to the “loading” cover-glass by their non-printing rPDMS “sticky” side.
Align the “loading” cover-glass horizontally or vertically to the microscope object table using a hand-made ruler and/or protractor.
Use DIC microscope with external monitor to align the nano-stamp to the pre-aligned “loading” cover-glass for precise horizontal or vertical positioning of the corresponding lines patterns.
Immobilize clean cut 1✕1 cm square “intermediate” cover-glasses to the glass-slide by scotch-tape.
Gently place vertically oriented nano-stamp with protein of interest #1 atop the immobilized cover-glass.
Align edges of “loading” cover-glass to the edges of the glass-slide with immobilized “intermediate” cover-glass.
Place a 100 gram weight on top of the “loading” cover-glass for 30 seconds.
Wet the bottom of the weight with a little amount of water before placing it on the cover-glass.
Gently remove the weight in one step together with the capillary effect-attached “loading cover-glass and the nano-stamp after 30 seconds.
Repeat the procedure with horizontally oriented nano-stamp coated with protein of interest #2.
Mix a 7-10 μL droplet of PAA with APS in the center of the freshly prepared thoroughly dried 3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl methacrylate-functionalized glass-bottom Petri dish.
Gently place “Intermediate” cover-glass with pre-printed nano-pattern face-down atop of the droplet to form a PAA “sandwich.”
Wait at least 20 minutes before going to the release step.
Gently release cover-glass from PAA gel by reversible hypotonic swelling in deionized Q-water (8-12 hours at +4°C or at 20-25°C for 40 minutes).
Optional: Ultrasonicate PAA gels in Q-water for ∼10-30 seconds if necessary.
Place released PAA nano-textures into isotonic PBS solution for 5 minutes.
Thoroughly rinse the PAA surfaces before utilization from cytotoxic sodium azide.
Incubate α-collagen-1 nano-lines sets with 1 mg/mL rat monomeric collagen type-I in cold PBS at +4°C for 8-24 hours, then rinse.
Incubate α-Fcγ Fab nano-lines sets with 200 μg/mL human E-cadherin-Fc chimeric protein in PBS solution at +4°C for 8-24 hours, then rinse.
